harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, /srv/data is now backed by a dedicated loop-backed LVM logical volume (datavg/datalv on /dev/loop0, XFS). Baseline app data was written, an LVM snapshot (datalv_snap) captured that state, /srv/data was then modified (a file deleted, a file overwritten, a file corrupted, an unexpected file added), and the LVM snapshot was merged back into the origin to restore the exact pre-modification content — verified via matching sha256 checksums. Persistence across reboot was arranged (systemd unit srvdata-loop-attach.service reattaches the loop device and activates the VG before local-fs mounting; /etc/fstab mounts /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv at /srv/data). The mandatory restart protocol was completed for node1: boot_id changed from f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c to 660dca51-3ccd-4408-a026-7b978e389d05, and post-reboot verification shows /srv/data auto-recovered with content identical to the snapshot baseline.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 storage: root is XFS on /dev/vda4 with no pre-existing LVM
Created a 2G loop-backed image file, built LVM PV/VG(datavg)/LV(datalv), formatted XFS, mounted at /srv/data
Populated baseline application data under /srv/data/app and recorded sha256 checksums
Created LVM snapshot datalv_snap of datalv capturing the baseline state
Modified /srv/data after the snapshot (deleted a file, rewrote config, corrupted payload, added an unexpected file) and confirmed checksums diverged from baseline
Restored via `lvconvert --merge` of datalv_snap into datalv; remounted and verified checksums exactly match baseline
Fixed /etc/fstab to mount /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv rather than a naive loop-file mount, which is incompatible with the LVM-on-loop layout

Created an idempotent systemd oneshot unit srvdata-loop-attach.service (enabled, WantedBy=sysinit.target, ordered before local-fs/lvm activation) to reattach the loop device and activate datavg at boot
Validated the boot sequence via a simulated cold-start cycle before rebooting
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy /srv/data checksums
Restarted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed
Verified post-reboot that the loop device, VG, and mount all came up automatically and /srv/data content matches the baseline checksums exactly

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before any changes
evidence.summary: Confirmed no existing LVM/snapshot capability, then built /srv/data on LVM and populated+checksummed baseline app data

evidence.requirement: Snapshot captures state prior to modification
evidence.summary: lvcreate -s created datalv_snap immediately after baseline checksums were recorded, before any modification
Post-snapshot modification (delete/overwrite/corrupt/add file) shown via diff against baseline checksums, proving divergence

evidence.requirement: Exact restoration of earlier snapshot content
evidence.summary: lvconvert --merge restored datalv from datalv_snap; post-restore checksums diffed against baseline with zero differences

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c and confirmed /srv/data checksums matched baseline immediately before reboot
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup; exec stream closed as node went down, confirming the restart was triggered

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: After polling through connection timeouts/resets, boot_id read as 660dca51-3ccd-4408-a026-7b978e389d05, differing from the pre-restart value
Post-reboot: srvdata-loop-attach.service active, loop device reattached, VG/LV active, /srv/data mounted, and checksums matched the snapshot-restored baseline exactly with zero diff
